title: Ellipse basics
brief: A 64-year-old with an 8 mm nodular BCC on the cheek. Excise it with a 4 mm margin and close the defect directly.
goals: Plan the excision: mark the lesion's margin, think about the direction of the skin tension lines (the RSTL compass).
Excise a fusiform ellipse around the margin and close it with sutures.

approach.text: A fusiform ellipse about 3 times as long as it is wide (30° tips), its long axis along the relaxed skin tension lines: the scar then lies in a line of least tension, and the length lets the ends close flat without dog-ears. Close from the middle outwards, halving the gaps.

tips.lesion: Keep the outline outside the margin circle all round: the margin is measured from the lesion's edge to the edge of the defect.
tips.closed: Close the whole length: a suture every few mm, starting in the middle and halving the gaps.
tips.tension: An ellipse across the tension lines closes under much more tension. Turn it along the RSTL compass.
tips.dog_ears: Short ellipses pucker at the ends. Aim for about 3:1 with 30° tips, or remove the dog-ears (Burow's triangles).
tips.sutures: A thread near its breaking strength will snap. Use a thicker thread, undermine, or reduce the tension with a better orientation.
